rationale: The claim is for accidental damage to a smartphone under Baggage and Personal Effects. The Economy plan has a per-item limit of $150 (section 1), which is lower than the claimed $1,099, making the eligible amount $150. The $100 deductible applies once per claim to Baggage and Personal Effects (section 1), leaving a payout of $50. The required documents (repair shop report and replacement receipt) are attached and support the claim.

The claim seeks payment for trip interruption because the insured left a child behind in Paris and returned home early. Under Section 2 of the policy, Trip Interruption is only payable for covered reasons such as sickness, severe weather, natural disaster, fire/flood making home uninhabitable, jury duty, or job loss. A parent's mistaken oversight is not a covered reason, so the claim is outside the scope of coverage.

The claim is referred because the required police report for the theft is missing. Policy Section 5 requires that theft must be reported to the local police within 24 hours and a copy of the police report is needed. The customer states they made a report but cannot locate it currently; the claim cannot proceed without this document. Additionally, the Economy plan has a $150 per-item limit which would cap the tablet ($450 claimed), rain jacket ($160 claimed), and sunglasses ($130 claimed), but the missing police report prevents assessment of the claim at this time.

The claim involves loss of prescription sunglasses allegedly stolen by a monkey, which would normally be covered under Section 5 (Baggage and Personal Effects). However, Section 5 requires that theft be reported to local police within 24 hours and a police report provided. The customer was unable to obtain a police report as local authorities do not handle monkey-related theft reports. The police report is a required document missing from this claim, necessitating referral to a colleague for further review.

The claim involves ambiguity under the "belongings left unattended" exclusion in section 5. The policy defines unattended as "out of your sight and out of your reach in a place the public can get to." While the phone was on a hotel soap shelf during the customer's shower (a place the public can access), it is unclear whether this momentary situation during normal travel activities constitutes "left unattended" as intended by the exclusion. Additionally, the Economy plan has a $150 per-item limit for electronics, which would cap any payout regardless. A colleague needs to evaluate the specific circumstances and policy interpretation.

The claim is for trip interruption due to the travelers realizing a child was left behind and choosing to return home early. Under section 2 (Trip Cancellation and Interruption), UnderCover only pays for interruption caused by covered reasons such as sickness, severe weather, natural disaster, home uninhabitability, jury duty, or job loss. The given reason (parental oversight/child left behind) is not a covered reason, and the policy explicitly states we do not pay for interruption for any other reason. Therefore the claim does not meet the policy's coverage criteria.

The claim involves a theft of baggage in Naples on July 14, 2026. The policy (section 5) requires a police report for theft claims, reporting within 24 hours. The customer submitted purchase receipts but not the police report; the report is mentioned as being in Italian and stored in trip paperwork. Since the police report is a required document missing from the claim, a colleague needs to follow up with the customer to obtain it before the claim can be assessed.

The claim is referred to a colleague because the policy requires a police report for theft claims under section 5 (Baggage and Personal Effects), but the local police at Uluwatu Temple refused to file a report for the monkey theft. The customer obtained a guide's letter instead, but the wording does not address the scenario where police decline to take a report. A colleague needs to determine whether an exception can be made or if the claim must be declined due to the missing police report.

The claim is for accidental damage to a smartphone during the covered trip (July 13, within July 10–17 trip dates). Section 5 covers accidental damage to personal belongings, and the repair shop report states the phone is beyond economical repair, satisfying the documentation requirement. Under the Economy plan, the per-item limit is $150 and the deductible is $100, so $150 − $100 = $50, which is within the $750 benefit maximum.

The trip interruption was caused by accidentally leaving a child at home, which is not one of the covered reasons listed in section 2 of the policy wording. None of the covered reasons (sickness/injury/death, severe weather, uninhabitable home or destination, jury duty/subpoena, job loss) apply to this situation, so the claim is not covered.

The claim is for theft of baggage and personal effects under Section 5. The Economy plan has a $750 benefit maximum, a $150 per-item limit, and a $100 deductible. A police report is explicitly required for theft claims under Section 5, but the customer states it is "somewhere in my paperwork" and will send it when found. This required document is missing, so per Section 11 the claim waits until it arrives. The sunglasses receipt is also absent from the submitted documents.

This is a theft claim under Baggage and Personal Effects (section 5). Section 5 requires that theft be reported to local police within 24 hours and that a copy of the police report be provided. The customer attempted to report to police at Uluwatu Temple but was told they do not take reports about monkeys, and instead provided a tour guide letter. Since the required police report is missing and the situation is unusual, a colleague needs to decide whether the guide letter is an acceptable substitute or whether the claim must be declined for lack of the required document.

The theft of baggage and personal effects during the covered trip is covered under Section 5. The incident occurred on July 6, 2026, within the trip dates (July 2-12, 2026), and a police report was filed the same day (within 24 hours as required). The Premium plan with Electronics Plus add-on applies: electronics per-item limit is $1,200 (covers headphones $429, e-reader $180, game console $399), and the tote bag ($95) is under the standard $300 per-item limit. Total eligible: $1,103. Less the $50 Premium deductible (applies once per claim to Baggage and Personal Effects per Section 1): payout $1,053, within the $1,500 benefit maximum.

The claim is for accidental damage to a smartphone during the covered trip. Under section 5 (Baggage and Personal Effects), accidental damage is covered with a repair estimate or statement that the item cannot be repaired; the repair shop report states the phone is beyond economical repair. The Economy plan has a per-item limit of $150 (section 1) and a $100 deductible that applies to Baggage and Personal Effects (section 1). The eligible amount is the lower of the claimed $1,099 and the per-item limit $150, minus the $100 deductible, resulting in a payout of $50. The incident occurred within the trip dates (July 10-17) and no exclusions apply.

The policy covers trip interruption only for the five reasons listed in section 2: sickness/injury/death of a traveler or family member, severe weather/natural disaster stopping carrier service for 24+ hours, home/destination uninhabitable due to fire/flood/storm, jury duty/court subpoena, or involuntary job loss after one year. The customer's reason—realizing mid-flight that a child was left at home—is not among these covered reasons. Section 2 explicitly states: "We do not pay for cancellation or interruption for any other reason." Therefore, the claim is not covered.

The claim is for theft of baggage and personal effects during the covered trip. The policy requires a police report for theft claims (section 5), which the customer indicates they have but have not yet provided. The claim must be referred until the police report is received. Additionally, the Economy plan has a $750 maximum and $150 per-item limit for Baggage and Personal Effects, and a $100 deductible applies once per claim. The tablet ($450) and rain jacket ($160) would be capped at $150 each, and the deductible would reduce the total payable amount.

The claim is for prescription sunglasses taken by a monkey at Uluwatu Temple. The First plan covers Baggage and Personal Effects up to $3,000 with a $500 per-item limit (Section 1). The incident occurred during the covered trip dates. However, the policy requires a police report for theft claims (Section 5), and the customer states the local police refused to file one for monkey incidents. A tour guide's letter is provided instead. It is unclear whether this event constitutes "theft" (requiring a police report), "loss" (no specific documentation stated), or "accidental damage" (requiring a repair estimate or statement of irreparability). Because the required police report is unobtainable and the policy does not address this situation, a colleague should review whether the guide's letter suffices as evidence and how to classify the incident.

The policy is Premium with Electronics Plus add-on. The theft occurred during the covered trip (July 2-12, 2026) and was reported to police within 24 hours with a police report provided. Electronics Plus raises the per-item limit for electronics to $1,200, so all three electronics items (headphones $429, e-reader $180, console $399) are fully covered. The tote bag ($95) is under the standard $300 per-item limit. Total eligible amount is $1,103. The $50 deductible for Premium plan applies once to Baggage and Personal Effects, leaving a payout of $1,053, which is under the $1,500 benefit maximum.

The claim is for a smartphone dropped in a hotel shower and damaged beyond repair. The incident occurred during the covered trip (July 13, 2026, within the July 10–17, 2026 trip dates). Under Section 5 (Baggage and Personal Effects), loss or accidental damage to personal belongings is covered, subject to the per-item limit and deductible. The policy is Economy plan with no add-ons, so the per-item limit is $150 (Section 1 table); the Electronics Plus add-on that would raise this to $1,200 is not present. The eligible amount is therefore the lower of the claimed $1,099 and the $150 per-item limit = $150. Section 10 step 3 requires subtracting the $100 deductible (which applies per claim to Baggage and Personal Effects). The result is $150 − $100 = $50, which is well below the $1,500 maximum for this benefit. The repair shop report and replacement receipt are provided and support the claim. The "unattended" exclusion in Section 5 does not apply because a hotel bathroom is not "a place the public can get to" as defined in the policy definitions.]

The claim is declined because the reason for trip interruption is not covered under Section 2 of the policy. The customer left their son Kevin behind at home due to oversleeping and a counting error, which is not one of the five covered reasons (sickness/injury/death, severe weather, uninhabitable home, jury duty, or job loss). Section 2 explicitly states: "We do not pay for cancellation or interruption for any other reason." The provided documents (airline receipt, hotel statement) are noted, but they do not change the fact that the underlying reason for the claim is excluded.

The claim is for baggage theft under Section 5, which requires a police report submitted within 24 hours of the incident. The customer reported making a report with the Carabinieri the next morning but does not currently have the police report document to submit. Since this is a required document per the policy, the claim cannot be processed until the police report is provided. Therefore, this requires a referral to a colleague.

This claim is referred because the required police report for theft is missing. Section 5 requires theft to be reported to local police within 24 hours with a copy of the police report. The local police at Uluwatu Temple declined to take a report about monkey theft, stating they do not handle such reports. Additionally, there are interpretive questions about whether this monkey incident constitutes "theft" or "loss" under the policy, and whether the "belongings left unattended" exclusion applies since the sunglasses were being worn at the time. A colleague needs to determine the proper categorization and whether an exception to the police report requirement is warranted given the circumstances.

The claim is for baggage theft under section 5. The incident occurred on July 6, 2026, within the covered trip dates (July 2–12, 2026). Theft was reported to local police within 24 hours, and a police report is provided. The claimant has receipts for all three electronics. With the Electronics Plus add-on, the per-item limit for electronics is $1,200; all three electronics ($429, $180, $399) are below this limit. The tote bag is $95, under the $300 per-item limit for the Premium plan. The deductible of $50 applies once per claim to Baggage and Personal Effects (section 10, step 3). The eligible amount is $1,103 (sum of all items), minus the $50 deductible equals $1,053, which is under the $1,500 maximum for the Premium plan. The bag was on the claimant's shoulder at the time of the snatching, so it was not "left unattended" (section 5 definition). The claim is approved.
